analysis: The PR only changes CI routing in .github/workflows/ci.yml and the matching docs in docs/developer/build.md. The single 'test-provider' lane with count 5 becomes five per-shard lanes (test-provider-1..5, count 1 each, lines 43-47). The test-provider job (line 143) now reads routes[format('test-provider-{0}', matrix.shard)]. Workflow permissions are unchanged: top-level contents: read, and the route job keeps permissions: {} (line 38). Checkout actions remain pinned. Release, signing, publication and cache-swift jobs still use literal Blacksmith labels (cache-swift at line 794). No secrets, new triggers, or untrusted-input interpolation were introduced; the new expressions use only needs.changes.outputs.provider compared to 'true' and matrix.shard, which is an integer. No provider runtime, coordinator protocol, attestation, key handling or prefix-cache code changed, so T-041 and the other threat-model entries are unaffected. Assumption not verifiable from the supplied evidence: darkbloom-route.yml (not supplied) must accept the new lane names, and it must still verify that a granted label matches the profile's exact Darkbloom labels (docs line ~256 states it does). A missing lane name would likely degrade into a failed or missing route rather than a security issue. Sandbox-plane grant semantics are outside this batch. Test jobs running on Darkbloom Macs have no release secrets in this workflow, since permissions are read-only. No security regression was identified.
